newsitem.title: USA: Boy undergoes world's first leg artery replacement.
newsitem.headline: Boy undergoes world's first leg artery replacement.

text.p: U.S. surgeons performed intricate artery replacement surgery on an 11-year-old boy on Tuesday in what doctors said was the first operation of its kind on a child in the world.

Christian Wood of Clifton Park, New York, was in surgery for 3 1/2 hours at Albany Medical Centre where a seven-member team of vascular surgeons replaced a missing piece of artery in his right leg with the synthetic material known as "Goretex."
"This procedure has been done in adults, but this is the first time it has been done in a child's leg," said Dr. Dhiraj Shah, head surgeon.
Dr. Shah and his team is already credited with performing 5,000 of these procedures on adults -- the world's largest number, hospital officials said.

During the procedure known as a "femoral-to-distal bypass," doctors replaced the absent artery with the graft -- two times bigger than the size of the tiny artery -- so the substitute artery will grow with the child.
"His right leg was not growing as big as the left and he couldn't do any athletics," said Dr. Shah, who has been a vascular surgeon for 25 years.
"He always had to stop and then limp because of poor circulation," the surgeon said.

After a recuperation period of four to six weeks, Dr. Shah said the surgery would allow the boy to participate in sports. The child was in good condition and was expected to be released from the hospital this weekend, Dr. Shah said.
